requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fingerprints`.

**SHA-256 over a word-based structural encoding.**
- `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` asserts that each Markdown fingerprint is 64 hex characters.
- `hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests` checks known SHA-256 vectors against the shared `Encoder` in `src/outline/hash.rs`, which every language uses. That test carries no `{test}` reference to the Markdown requirement. It does reference the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, and the digest code is language-independent, so I do not count it as a gap.
- The word-boundary tests below also exercise the encoding.

**Fingerprint scheme.** `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` asserts `markdown-structural-v1` for `languages::Markdown`. It checks both the language's `fingerprint_scheme()` and the scheme that `OutlineContent` retains. The scheme requirement is cited here, so it is context only.

**HTML comment blocks excluded.**
- `comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile` has a Markdown case. Changing the comment text, or removing the `<!-- note -->` block, leaves the `section[H]` hash equal. Changing the prose word changes the hash.
- `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` has the same Markdown scenario.
- `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` shows that only the block is treated as a comment.

**Inline HTML comments stay paragraph text.**
- The final assertion in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` changes the text inside `<!-- one -->` within a paragraph and requires a different fingerprint.
- `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` asserts that the owner of an inline-comment line is a `paragraph`.

**Word-based hashing and reflow for paragraphs.**
- `reflowing_markdown_paragraphs_keeps_the_hash` checks that line-break changes preserve the hash and that `brownfox` differs from `brown fox`.
- `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` checks that `ab cd` differs from `abcd` and that `  ab\ncd  ` equals `ab cd`.
- `markdown_hashes_include_paragraph_text_between_punctuation_tokens` checks that added words change the hash and that extra spaces do not.
- `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates` checks that reflowing a paragraph and a nested directive keeps the node hash, and that replacing the text changes it.

**Directive prose.** `directive_prose_hashes_words_across_reflow_without_joining_them` checks that reflow and extra spaces keep the fingerprint of a `block` node and that `twowords` changes it.

Together these cover the positive and negative cases for each obligation: preserving the hash on reflow, changing it on word changes, excluding block comments, and keeping inline comments. I found no unmet obligation or assertion gap.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
